question: Why did Argentine ants stop fighting neighbouring nests once they spread beyond South America?
answer: They lost the genetic variety that marks strangers. Few founders reached California, so nests there share nearly the same scent labels and treat each other as kin. Freed from border wars, they merge into supercolonies; one runs about 6,000 km along the coasts of southern Europe, its nests accepting one another throughout.
move: A group that cannot tell outsiders apart may grow stronger, not weaker.
reference: Tsutsui, Suarez, Holway & Case, Reduced genetic variation and the success of an invasive species, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2000
